candidate.signature: (two finite acyclic first-order ground terms)->(canonical variable-labeled least general generalization, substitutions to each input)
candidate.law: Given two finite acyclic ground first-order terms over exact constructor/arity and constant identities, return their least general generalization (lgg) under syntactic substitutions. Identical symbols/constructors retain identity; identical function symbol and arity recurse by argument. A divergent ordered pair of subterms maps to one fresh variable shared in ALL occurrences of the SAME ordered pair; distinct divergent pairs receive distinct variables. Canonical variable labels assigned by first left-to-right preorder encounter, starting V0. Preserve substitutions mapping result to the two inputs. No theory of associativity/commutativity and no lambda binding are admitted.
candidate.profile: Atom=nonempty string, compound=[functor_string,arg1,...argN], N>=1, no variable input; output diverging variable represented as {'var':nonnegative int}; input dictionaries, cyclic trees, non-ground terms and higher-order functions excluded.

witnesses.reason: repeated disagreement pair must share one variable
distinct ordered pairs must NOT be fused
nested reuse of same term pair
functor mismatch replaces the entire subtree
exact equal terms preserve their structure

falsifiers: A single variable for two distinct ordered mismatches may prevent reproducing both inputs.
Fresh variable per repeated ordered mismatch loses the most-specific substitution-sharing law.
Ignoring constructor arity or symbol differences invents false common structure.
Changing child order or treating + as commutative changes the unadmitted syntactic theory.
formal_obligations: Instance witness: both inputs are exact substitution instances of lgg.
Leastness: any common syntactic generalization subsumes lgg (up to variable renaming).
Canonical renaming stable under source swap (same shape, first-occurrence variable numbering).
Behavioral dedup with ratified D9 UNIFY, EXPLAIN-PROOF and selected D10 RENAME-VARS / PROVE-RULE; inverse relation does NOT prove Core independence.
